original_title: [177Lu]Lu-Prostate-specific Membrane Antigen Radioligand Therapy Combined With a PARP Inhibitor in Treatment-emergent Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer With Rare Metastases: A New Try.
title: Adding a PARP inhibitor when prostate cancer stops acting like prostate cancer
blurb: A combo attempt pairing Lu-177-PSMA radioligand therapy with a PARP inhibitor in treatment-emergent neuroendocrine prostate cancer that's picked up rare metastatic sites, the kind of transformed disease where PSMA-RLT alone was never going to be enough. Reads like a single case or small series, so treat it as hypothesis-generating rather than practice-changing.

original_title: Catalytic enantioselective dual C–H cross-coupling enabled by a radical-buffering strategy
title: A radical-buffering trick lets one catalyst run two C–H couplings at once
blurb: Dual C–H cross-coupling done enantioselectively, with a radical-buffering strategy keeping the radical intermediate in line long enough to control the stereochemistry instead of racing off and scrambling it. Nature Synthesis, so presumably vetted, but still one paper.

original_title: Personalized dosimetry for targeted radionuclide therapy: initial clinical experience from a case series at a tertiary cancer center (King Hussein Cancer Center).
title: Dosimetry gets personal, one case series at a time
blurb: A case series out of King Hussein Cancer Center walking through personalized dosimetry for targeted radionuclide therapy. Early clinical experience, not a trial, so it's a proof the workflow runs in practice rather than evidence it changes outcomes.
venue: Q J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

original_title: Transglutaminase 1 is conserved in amphibians and required for membrane-associated transglutaminase activity in the epidermis of clawed frogs
title: Frogs kept the skin-glue enzyme humans can't live without
blurb: TGM1 cross-links proteins to harden mammalian skin, and losing it kills mice and causes a skin disease in people. The gene is conserved across all three amphibian lineages, anurans, caudates, and caecilians, with the catalytic residues intact in the clawed frog, so whatever TGM1 does for cornification predates the mammal-amphibian split by a long way.

original_title: Development and Preclinical Evaluation of 68Ga-Labeled BCMA-Targeting Nanobodies for PET Imaging of Multiple Myeloma
title: Three BCMA nanobodies for myeloma PET, and none of them wins outright
blurb: Three 68Ga-labeled nanobodies against BCMA, affinities all double-digit nanomolar but ranging from 33 to 87 nM depending on the clone. C07 binds tightest at 33 nM yet shows the weakest tumor uptake and weakest blocking, while C02 has the loosest affinity at 58 nM but the best uptake and near-best blocking. Tight binding didn't translate into getting into the tumor, which is the actually useful finding here.

original_title: Concise and Modular Access to a Chiral Biaryl Monophosphine Library and Downstream Use in Catalytic Enantioselective Transformations
title: A three-step shortcut to the chiral ligands everyone resolves by hand
blurb: Atropoisomeric biaryl monophosphines, the chiral cousins of Buchwald ligands, are usually made by resolution or long step counts that kill structural diversity. This route builds a tunable library in three steps, starting from an atroposelective Ir(III)-catalyzed C–H arylation of a phosphine oxide. More variants to actually screen instead of just whatever you can resolve.

original_title: Copper-catalyzed doubly enantioconvergent radical C(sp3)–P cross-coupling for the construction of P- and P,C-stereogenic centers
title: Copper closes in on P- and P,C-stereocenters at once
blurb: A copper-catalyzed radical C(sp3)–P cross-coupling that's doubly enantioconvergent, meaning it takes racemic starting material and still lands cleanly on P- and P,C-stereogenic centers. In Chem, light on detail beyond that.

original_title: Optimization of the Arg8−Arg9 Cleavage Site in 68Ga-Labeled Neurotensin(6−13) Analogs for NTSR1-Targeted PET Imaging of Cancer
title: Patching the weak link in neurotensin PET tracers
blurb: NTSR1-targeting PET tracers built on neurotensin keep getting chewed up by proteases, especially at three specific peptide bonds. This work goes after just the Arg8-Arg9 site, swapping in non-canonical amino acids across a series of DOTA-conjugates to block the cut while keeping receptor affinity. The other two cleavage sites are still sitting there unaddressed.

original_title: Emerging trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2-targeting antibody-drug conjugates in gynecological cancers
title: TROP-2 ADCs reach for gynecological cancers next
blurb: TROP-2 sits barely expressed on normal tissue but overexpressed in endometrial, ovarian, and cervical cancer, the usual setup for an antibody-drug conjugate pitch. A review rounding up the TROP-2 ADCs now being aimed at gynecologic cancer specifically, not new data of its own.

original_title: Automated Synthesizer Validates Terbium-161 Radioligand Production for Advanced Prostate Cancer Therapy - Bioengineer.org
title: Terbium-161 radioligand production, now on autopilot
blurb: An automated synthesizer validated for producing Terbium-161 radioligands aimed at advanced prostate cancer, per a write-up on Bioengineer.org. Long on the word 'validates,' short on actual numbers, so I'd want the underlying paper before getting excited.

original_title: Development and Preclinical Evaluation of Six-Transmembrane Epithelial Antigen of Prostate 2 Targeted PET Probes: A Case of Drug Repurposing Based on Molecular Docking.
title: Repurposing old drugs as STEAP2 PET probes via docking
blurb: STEAP2-targeted PET probes built by screening existing drugs through molecular docking rather than designing new chemistry from scratch. Preclinical development and evaluation only, in J Med Chem, for imaging prostate cancer.

original_title: Electro‐Biocatalytic Dearomative Oxidation–Asymmetric Aldol Cascade Enables Direct Synthesis of Chiral 3‐Hydroxyindolin‐2‐Ones From Indoles
title: Electricity and an enzyme share one pot to build chiral oxindoles
blurb: Electrochemical dearomatization of indole feeds straight into a CALB-catalyzed aldol in the same vessel, no intermediate workup, and the enzyme still delivers solid diastereo- and enantioselectivity on the 3-hydroxyindolin-2-one product. Tested across a decent range of substituted indoles plus two cyclic ketones, so it's not riding on one lucky substrate.

original_title: Trifluoromethanesulfonyl‐Based Reagents: Novel Synthetic Strategies and Mechanistic Insights for Trifluoromethylation Transformations
title: A review of what triflyl reagents can actually do for CF3 chemistry
blurb: A survey of trifluoromethanesulfonyl-based reagents, tracking how they've been pushed into site-selective, scalable trifluoromethylation and the mechanisms behind those transformations. A map of the field, not a single new result.

original_title: Elucidation of Pathways in the Conversion of CO2-Rich Syngas to Methanol over Cu-Based Catalysts
title: Why CuZnZr wins at turning CO2-heavy syngas into methanol
blurb: Across a series of Cu catalysts run on syngas with CO2 content from 4 to 25%, CuZnZr comes out on top, and the paper actually explains why: a strengthened Cu-oxide interaction plus a better Cu-ZnO-ZrOx interface that helps grab and activate both CO and CO2. Mechanistic insight, not just a leaderboard.

original_title: Direct catalytic formation of styrene from acetylene
title: Turning acetylene straight into styrene, skipping benzene
blurb: Acetylene would much rather cyclotrimerize into benzene, which is why a direct route to styrene has never existed. This gets there anyway on a single earth-abundant metal center, intercepting that cyclotrimerization step and marrying it to alkyne hydroarylation before it can finish into benzene. Styrene's a >30 Mt/year commodity made by energy-intensive routes today, so a direct C2 shortcut is worth watching, assuming it gets past one metal center in a flask.

original_title: Controlled crosslink cleavage and phase separation enable highly stretchable and strong 3D-printed hydrogel for soft robotics.
title: 3D-printed hydrogels that are both stretchy and tough, for soft robots
blurb: Controlled crosslink cleavage paired with phase separation gets a 3D-printed hydrogel that's unusually stretchable and strong at the same time, a combination soft robotics usually has to pick one of.

original_title: Synthesis and In Vitro/In Vivo Stability Evaluation of Various Radioiodinated Tyrosine Derivatives.
title: Stress-testing radioiodinated tyrosine tracers before anyone injects one
blurb: A set of radioiodinated tyrosine derivatives put through in vitro and in vivo stability testing, the unglamorous but necessary step before any of them earns the word tracer.

original_title: Deciphering Charge Delocalization across Mercaptobenzonitrile Ligand Terminals and Inner Hydrides in Atomically Precise Cu14H10 Nanoclusters for Electrocatalytic CO2 Reduction
title: Mapping where the charge actually sits in a Cu14H10 hydride cluster
blurb: Atomically precise Cu hydride clusters are a pain to characterize since finding the hydrides usually needs single crystals and a neutron beam, and the clusters themselves are UV-vis-shy and electrochemically twitchy. This Cu14H10 cluster, capped with mercaptobenzonitrile and triphenylphosphine ligands, gets mapped anyway, tracing charge delocalization between the ligand terminals and the buried hydrides, with CO2 reduction catalysis as the point of the exercise.

original_title: Photosensitized Synthesis of 1,2-Iminosulfides via β-Fragmentation of Bifunctional Oxime Reagents
title: One oxime reagent, two radicals, one new bond
blurb: A bifunctional oxime ester spits out a thiyl and an iminyl radical from the same molecule, with an ethylene linker quietly keeping the thiol's electronics from getting in the way of photoactivation before it fragments off. Runs under mild organophotocatalysis across a range of thiols to build the beta-iminosulfides. Clever reagent design hiding behind a dull name.

original_title: Semi-Quantitative In Vivo Imaging of Intratumorally Injected Iodine-125-Labeled Nanoparticles Using a Benchtop 2D Multi-Pinhole X-ray System
title: A benchtop X-ray rig that can actually find your I-125 nanoparticles
blurb: PEG-coated gold-core, silver-shell nanoparticles carrying iodine-125 get tracked in vivo after intratumoral injection using a 2D multi-pinhole X-ray setup built around a cadmium zinc telluride detector, calibrated to read activity out semi-quantitatively on a benchtop rig rather than needing a full imaging suite. Useful if you're doing nano-brachytherapy and actually want to confirm the dose landed where you aimed it.

original_title: Concise and Modular Access to a Chiral Biaryl Monophosphine Library and Downstream Use in Catalytic Enantioselective Transformations
title: A three-step shortcut to atrop-chiral Buchwald-type ligands
blurb: Biaryl monophosphine ligands are normally stuck with resolution or long step counts, which kills any real exploration of the ligand space. This swaps in a Cp*-Ir(III)-catalyzed atroposelective C-H arylation of a phosphine oxide as the key step, gets a broadly tunable ligand library in three steps, and then actually puts them to work in asymmetric catalysis instead of stopping at the synthesis paper.

original_title: Chemical emulation of the biosynthesis of (±)-arnebidin
title: Arnebidin's cyclopropane cage, built the way biology might have
blurb: A biosynthesis-inspired Diels-Alder cascade gets to the first total synthesis of (±)-arnebidin in 13 steps, snapping together its cyclopropane-studded seven-ring frame at room temperature. Doubles as evidence for the proposed biosynthetic route, not just a synthesis flex.

original_title: Site-specific field comparison of in situ NaI(Tl) gamma-ray spectrometry for ambient dose equivalent rate estimation and <sup>137</sup>Cs spectral screening
title: Field-testing gamma detectors against Cs-137, not just the lab bench
blurb: A site-specific field comparison of in-situ NaI(Tl) gamma spectrometers for ambient dose rate estimation and Cs-137 screening. Unglamorous, but this is the calibration legwork that keeps dose numbers trustworthy.

original_title: Aryl radical buffering facilitates asymmetric dual C–H cross-coupling
title: Taming aryl radicals long enough to pair them up asymmetrically
blurb: Buffering aryl radicals apparently keeps them well-behaved enough to run a dual C-H cross-coupling with asymmetric control, a combination that's usually too unruly to steer.

original_title: Acid-Induced Intramolecular Transformations in Mixed Phosphonium–Iodonium Ylides with a Dibenzothiaphosphonium Core
title: This ylide would rather swap iodobenzene for water
blurb: Acid treatment of a dibenzothiaphosphonium-based phosphonium-iodonium ylide kicks out iodobenzene and pulls in water instead, landing sulfonium salts in up to 93% yield. The oxygen-bridged version does the opposite and ring-expands, so the swap is the point. The sulfonium forms as the wrong diastereomer first and slowly flips to the stable one by S-inversion, which they clocked with variable-temperature NMR and DFT.

original_title: Synthesis and Preclinical Evaluation of a Novel Technetium-99m-Labeled Tracer for Tumor Hypoxia Imaging with Low Uptake in the Intestines and Liver.
title: A hypoxia tracer that doesn't light up your gut instead of the tumor
blurb: A new Tc-99m-labeled tracer for imaging tumor hypoxia, preclinical so far, whose selling point is low background uptake in the intestines and liver, which is usually what ruins the read on these scans.

original_title: An N-Heterocyclic Imine-Supported Two-Coordinate 1,2-Bis(borinium) Dication
title: A diboron dication with no babysitters
blurb: An N-heterocyclic imine props up a two-coordinate 1,2-bis(borinium) dication built on a bare B(sp)-B(sp) bond, no donor ligand, no counterion, no solvent molecule anywhere near it. These are supposed to be too electron-poor and too repulsive to isolate, so getting one to just sit there in a crystal is the whole story.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Synthesis of [1,4]Oxazino[3,2- e ][1,2,4]triazines by One-Pot Cascade Regioselective Substitutions of 3,5,6-Trichloro-1,2,4-triazine with Amino Alcohols
title: Trichlorotriazine, one pot, a pile of new oxazino-triazines
blurb: Cheap amino alcohols plus 3,5,6-trichloro-1,2,4-triazine in a regioselective one-pot cascade churns out a broad set of oxazino-triazines fast, off cheap reagents. They also ran the postsynthetic scope through HTE and strung together a three-step cascade to show you can reach a fully dressed-up triazine in one pot.

original_title: Photoredox/Chiral Brønsted-Acid-Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrofluoroalkylation of α,β-Unsaturated Amides with Langlois-Type Reagents
title: Fluoroalkyl amides made chiral with light and a Brønsted acid
blurb: Photoredox paired with a chiral Brønsted acid turns Langlois-type sulfinates into fluoroalkyl radicals, CF3 up through C4F9, that add asymmetrically to unsaturated amides, up to 99% yield and 96:4 e.r. The stereocontrol survives even with water around, so these normally finicky inorganic sulfinates still work in a mostly nonpolar medium. Mechanism points to reductive quenching, radical addition, then a stereocontrolled protonation.

original_title: Oriented macrocycles as design elements in molecular machines
title: Macrocycles that know which way they're facing
blurb: A look at using oriented macrocycles as design elements for molecular machines. Not much more on offer than the concept itself.

original_title: Molecular Imaging of Liver Fibrosis using [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT: A Prospective head-to-head comparison with Transient Elastography, Serum Biomarkers & Metavir Histopathological Staging
title: Ga-68 FAPI-04 PET against the actual liver fibrosis workup
blurb: A prospective head-to-head of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT against transient elastography, serum biomarkers, and Metavir histopathology staging for liver fibrosis. It's the direct comparison against the real clinical standards, not another tracer study floating on its own, that makes this one worth reading.

original_title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Ion-Association Design Decouples Linearity and Dynamic Range in Organic Electrochemical Synapses
title: AI picks the ions to break a neuromorphic transistor trade-off
blurb: Organic electrochemical synapses usually force a choice between linear weight updates and wide dynamic range, because uncontrolled interface doping kinetics couple the two. This uses an AI-assisted binary-electrolyte ion-association design to decouple them instead of just trading one for the other. Early days for what's effectively an electrolyte search problem, but if it generalizes it's a real lever for these devices.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Asymmetric Synthesis of a Small Molecule Inhibitor of TNFα via Enantioenriched 4-Substituted Tetrahydroisoquinolines
title: A TNFα inhibitor route that ditches the column
blurb: A chromatography-free asymmetric route to a TNFα inhibitor lead, scaled to over 20 g with a greater than 15-fold yield improvement over the original synthesis. The real engineering is the Parham cyclization scaling to hectogram quantities of the dihydroisoquinolone intermediate, which is what turns an academic route into a process.

original_title: Ring Expansion of Carbocycles via Heteroatom‐Enabled Skeletal Editing
title: Five years of stuffing nitrogen and oxygen into carbocycle rings
blurb: A review covering 2020-2025 progress on expanding carbocycles into heterocycles by inserting nitrogen or oxygen atoms into the ring, skeletal editing rather than the usual peripheral functional-group tweaking. Handy as a map of the field, but it's a survey, not a new reaction.

original_title: Breaking the “Micro-Size Inversion” Paradox via a Surface-Chemistry-Driven Molecular Sieving Membrane for Ambient Lithium–Air Batteries
title: Letting O2 through while blocking the smaller water molecule
blurb: Ambient-air lithium-air batteries need O2 in and H2O out, but water (0.275 nm) is actually smaller than O2 (0.346 nm), so plain pore-size sieving can't separate them. They graft fluorinated chains onto a vinyl-functionalized covalent organic framework and pair it with PDMS to sieve by surface chemistry instead of size. A real fix for a problem that's been quietly sabotaging open-air Li-air cells.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Computational study of B–B single-bond formation between a cage-localised carboranyl radical and DMAc-activated bis(catecholato)diboron: a concerted but asynchronous B–B bond-forming step with barrierless DMAc release
title: Mapping the fiddly B-B bond step behind a BNCT building block
blurb: DFT work on how a carboranyl radical adds to DMAc-activated bis(catecholato)diboron to forge the B-B bond in a scalable route to boron-rich constructs for boron neutron capture therapy. The potential surface is so flat that standard saddle-point searches fail to converge, concerted but asynchronous, with DMAc release coming off barrierless. Explains why this step is temperamental rather than reporting anything new to make.

original_title: Dimeric Cu(I) Hydride‐Catalyzed Alkene Hydrogenation and Imine Olefination: Mechanistic Insights Into Stereocontrol
title: Why the copper dimer, not the monomer, runs the reaction
blurb: DFT on CuH-catalyzed reductive coupling of activated alkenes with imines finds the dinuclear copper hydride is both more stable than the monomer and so sterically packed it forces an outer-sphere hydrogen migration, generating the key anionic intermediate before it ever meets the imine. A mechanism paper explaining the stereocontrol, not a new transformation.

original_title: Iridium‐Catalyzed Borane Reduction of Esters for the Construction of Sterically Hindered and α , α ‐Dideuterated Ethers
title: An iridium catalyst reduces esters to ethers silanes can't reach
blurb: A square-planar Ir(I) dicarbonyl complex with a p-toluidine ligand, paired with cheap BH3·DMS, reduces esters straight to hindered ethers, including α-tertiary and neopentylic β-quaternary cases existing silane-based methods can't touch. It also delivers site-specific α,α-dideuterated versions, which matters if you need the deuterium exactly there rather than scattered across the molecule.

original_title: Influence of Fluorine Substitution Pattern in Arylboronic Acid Caps on the Myocardial Perfusion Imaging Properties of Technetium Monocapped Tris(dioxime) Complexes.
title: Tuning the fluorine on a heart-imaging technetium tracer's cap
blurb: Looks at how shifting the fluorine substitution pattern on arylboronic acid caps changes myocardial perfusion imaging performance in technetium monocapped tris(dioxime) complexes. Cap chemistry is usually what decides biodistribution and clearance in these tracers, so that's the part worth getting right.

original_title: Engineering a C─N Lyase for Enantioselective Hydroaminations With Secondary Amines
title: Teaching an aspartase-family lyase to finally take secondary amines
blurb: C-N lyases from the aspartase/fumarase superfamily normally refuse secondary amines, so an engineered EDDS lyase variant (Y26A/Q159V/R294E) is made to do enantioselective hydroamination with them anyway, a 20-fold activity jump over wild type. Opens up noncanonical amino acid synthesis beyond the primary-amine-only scope these enzymes were stuck with.

original_title: A SPECT-Guided, PET-Sparing Algorithm for PSMA Radiopharmaceutical Therapy Evaluation (SPARE)
title: Skipping the PET scan when checking on PSMA radioligand therapy
blurb: An algorithm (SPARE) that substitutes SPECT for PET when evaluating how patients are doing on PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy, easing reliance on PET slots that are often harder to book.

original_title: Beyond AlphaFold 3: a standardised benchmark of open-source co-folding models for antibody–antigen complexes, from docking accuracy to interaction specificity
title: Benchmarking the AlphaFold 3 challengers on antibody-antigen docking
blurb: A standardized shootout of open-source co-folding models against each other on antibody-antigen complexes, scored on docking accuracy and whether they actually get the interaction specificity right, not just a plausible-looking fold. Useful mainly for knowing which free model to trust before you pay for AlphaFold 3.

original_title: From Sintering to Mineralization: A Liquid-Phase Growth Route for Ceramic Films
title: Growing ceramic films from solution instead of baking them
blurb: Dense ceramic films usually force a bad trade: hot enough to sinter also means hot enough to boil off elements and segregate phases. This biomimetic liquid-phase growth route borrows mineralization chemistry to grow dense films under mild conditions instead, tested on the stubbornly refractory proton conductor BZY. If it generalizes past that one system, it's a real fix for the sintering dilemma.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Non-halogen aqueous electrolytes for four-electron iodine conversion
title: Four-electron iodine chemistry without the corrosive halogen soup
blurb: Reversible four-electron iodine redox for aqueous metal-iodine batteries has always needed concentrated, corrosive interhalogen electrolytes to keep the hypervalent iodine stable. This swaps that for a kosmotropic anion/polar anion/nucleophile framework that stabilizes the interface without any halogen additives. Energy density without the hazmat sheet, if the stability holds past the lab cell.

original_title: Nonlinear Field-Reorganization Coupling Dictates Cation-Steered Proton Transfer at Electrified Interfaces
title: Cations are steering protons straight to CO2, skipping a step
blurb: AIMD simulations find that cations parked in the double layer don't just tweak CO2 reduction at the margins, they set up a local field that yanks protons directly onto adsorbed CO2 via an Eley-Rideal path, bypassing the usual Volmer hydrogen-adsorption step entirely. That's a specific mechanistic claim for why cation choice matters in CO2RR, not just another correlation.

original_title: Water-Mediated Electrochemical Oxidative Dearomatization of Indoles: A Sustainable Approach to 2-Hydroxyindolin-3-ones
title: Water does the oxidizing in this indole dearomatization
blurb: An electrochemical, metal-free route dearomatizes indoles into 2-hydroxyindolin-3-ones, with water supplying both the new hydroxyl and the carbonyl oxygen rather than some stoichiometric oxidant. Isotope labeling and D2O experiments back up where the oxygen actually comes from, and it builds a C2 quaternary center along the way, which is usually the annoying part.

original_title: Mesh-based detailed human kidney models of the ICRP reference adults for radiopharmaceutical therapy dosimetry: microscale model of the renal cortex.
title: A mesh model of the kidney down to the cortex's microstructure
blurb: A detailed mesh-based human kidney model built to ICRP reference-adult specs, now with a microscale model of the renal cortex for radiopharmaceutical dosimetry. The kind of unglamorous anatomical plumbing that determines whether your dose estimates to the kidney are actually trustworthy.

original_title: Photocatalytic Cascade Radical Sulfonamidation/Cyclization of N -Isopentenyl Aldehyde Hydrazones to Access C5-Sulfonamidated Tetrahydropyridazines
title: Photocatalysis builds sulfonamidated tetrahydropyridazines in one cascade
blurb: A photoinduced radical cascade using 4CzIPN sticks the sulfonylamino group onto the ring carbon (C5) rather than the side chain, turning N-isopentenyl hydrazones into tetrahydropyridazines in 61-87% yield. The selectivity for ring over chain is the actual result here.

original_title: Transition‐Metal‐Free Methylation of Arylboronates with Tuneable Deuterium Incorporation
title: Methylating arylboronates without a transition metal, deuterium optional
blurb: The 'magic methyl' trick for improving drug PK/PD usually means a transition-metal catalyst, which also makes deuteromethylation annoying. This method methylates arylboronates with no metal catalyst and lets you dial the deuterium content on the incoming group, which is exactly what you want when fine-tuning metabolic stability.

original_title: Electrochemical and Photochemical Transformations of Tertiary Formamides
title: A review of what electro- and photochemistry can do to tertiary formamides
blurb: Tertiary formamides have no N-H and plenty of steric bulk around the nitrogen, so they've traditionally needed stoichiometric oxidants or harsh nucleophiles to budge. This review rounds up the decade's worth of electrochemical and photochemical methods that activate them instead, a catalog piece rather than a new result.

original_title: Polymorphism and Dimensionality in Rhodium Chalcogenide Nanocrystals
title: Rhodium chalcogenide nanocrystals, now in four different shapes
blurb: A colloidal route finally gets at rhodium chalcogenides' nanocrystal chemistry, which had been mostly unexplored in solution. Tuning the precursor and injection/growth temperatures switches between Rh0.78Se, 2D and 3D RhTe2, and Rh3Te8, all air-stable at 5-30 nm. The dimensionality control by synthesis knobs alone is the part worth noting.

original_title: Crystal-field modulation activates dormant tetrahedral Co sites for efficient alkaline hydrogen evolution
title: An acid wash wakes up dormant cobalt sites for hydrogen evolution
blurb: Oxalic acid strips just enough off the surface of spinel Co3O4 to activate tetrahedral Co sites that were otherwise sitting idle, without wrecking the crystal structure. The result needs only 38 mV to hit 10 mA/cm² in 1 M KOH and keeps that up for 1000 hours, which is the stability number alkaline HER catalysts don't usually get to claim.

original_title: Photochemical CF 3 Radical Generation: A Spin Trapping/Electron Paramagnetic Resonance and In Situ 19 F Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Study
title: Who's actually generating the CF3 radical
blurb: Umemoto and Togni reagents get used constantly to bolt CF3 groups onto molecules, but how they actually spit out the radical has stayed vague. This runs 18 different CF3-donor reagents through spin-trapping EPR and in situ 19F NMR to watch it happen directly instead of inferring it from products.

original_title: Enzyme‐Functionalized Microparticles to Open the Vitreoretinal Interface
title: Enzyme-coated microparticles pry open the eye's toughest membrane
blurb: The inner limiting membrane blocks almost everything but the smallest nanoparticles from reaching the retina. Enzyme-decorated microcolloids locally open that membrane so passive carriers can diffuse through afterward, a workaround for getting past the ILM rather than a fix for intravitreal delivery generally.

original_title: Reverse Water Gas Shift Reaction over a Homogeneous Iron Catalyst and the Underlying Mechanism
title: An iron catalyst runs reverse water-gas shift without the heat
blurb: RWGS usually means heterogeneous catalysts above 600°C and still poor CO selectivity below 400°C, and the homogeneous options on record have mostly been noble metals. Iron phthalocyanine does it homogeneously at low temperature instead, a cheap metal with the mechanism worked out alongside it.

original_title: Ligand Rollover C-H Activation as a Strategy for Intermolecular C-H Activation
title: A platinum complex activates its own ligand to make a point about C-H bonds elsewhere
blurb: Heating a Pt(II) complex with an NNNO pyridine ligand in C6D6 at 100°C hands a deuterium from solvent to methane and leaves a deuterated isoxazolyl group behind, the signature of ligand rollover C-H activation happening intramolecularly. The claim is that this metal-ligand-cooperative trick can be turned outward to activate C-H bonds in other molecules, not just the ligand itself.

original_title: Engineered interface in sunlight-driven non-oxidative ethane dehydrogenation
title: Full-spectrum sunlight, no oxidant, just ethane losing its hydrogens
blurb: Non-oxidative alkane dehydrogenation needs a lot of activation energy, which most of the solar spectrum can't supply. A surface modification on TiN adds interfacial sites that keep strong light absorption while also helping electron-hole pairs recombine productively there, so the reaction runs across the full spectrum instead of just the high-energy end.

original_title: Nanobodies in precision oncology from target recognition to tumor-state-matched therapy
title: Nanobodies grow up into actual cancer therapies
blurb: A review on camelid single-domain antibodies as their own design space rather than shrunken monoclonal antibodies: small, stable, easy to engineer, with fast tumor penetration, fast clearance, modular multivalency, fusions, and radionuclide conjugation all on the table. The pitch is matching the nanobody format to the tumor's actual state rather than running one format for everything.

original_title: Stimuli-Responsive Viologen-Based Coordination Supramolecular Isomers Modulated by π-Stacking Interactions
title: Same copper complex, two crystal personalities, just from how it stacks
blurb: Two CuCl2(PhSQ)2 isomers built from identical pieces come out structurally different depending on how π-stacking between the viologen-based ligands lines up, with one forming an extended stacked framework. Packing-induced supramolecular isomers are supposedly rare because packing is hard to control on purpose, so landing a matched pair like this is the actual result here.

original_title: Enhanced Propane Dehydroaromatization over CeZn/ZSM-5 Nanosheets
title: Shrinking a zeolite's b-axis so propane dehydroaromatization stops choking on carbon
blurb: Zn/ZSM-5 catalysts for turning propane into aromatics keep dying from carbon buildup because the long diffusion path traps everything inside the channels. A urea-assisted hydrothermal method shortens that b-axis well below the usual 250-270 nm, and the thinner CeZn/ZSM-5 nanosheets hold up noticeably better as a result.

original_title: The Structural Twist of His1 Residue in Cu-ATCUN Metallopeptides: A Rule Breaker on Redox Activity
title: Move one histidine and a 'redox-silent' copper peptide turns active
blurb: The whole reputation of the ATCUN motif rests on its tight square-planar Cu(II) complex being unable to take up Cu(I), so it just sits there redox-inactive. Put a histidine in the first position instead of the canonical residue and that rule breaks, and comparing canonical, modified, and acetylated versions of the peptide tracks exactly how that structural twist flips redox activity on.

original_title: Study Finds Antibody–Drug Conjugate Safety Profiles Differ by Platform and Target - Bioengineer.org
title: ADC side effects depend on which platform you built it on
blurb: A survey across antibody-drug conjugates finds the safety profile tracks the delivery platform and the target, not just the drug class. Useful to see it laid out systematically rather than assumed.

original_title: A Quantitative Map of Boryl Substituent Effects Through Hammett Parameters and Electronic Analysis
title: Finally some real Hammett numbers for boryl groups
blurb: Boryl groups show up everywhere in modern synthesis but their electronic effects were only quantified for a handful of them. This pairs acidity measurements on meta- and para-substituted benzoic acids with computation to build out Hammett constants for the common boryl substituents. A reference table dressed up as a paper, but a reference table the field actually needed.

original_title: Radiopharma player PharmaLogic snaps up Lantheus' CDMO business, plant as Curium acquisition advances - Fierce Pharma
title: PharmaLogic picks up Lantheus' CDMO arm while the Curium deal rolls on
blurb: Lantheus sells its contract manufacturing business and plant to PharmaLogic, timed right alongside the ongoing Curium acquisition. Radiopharma consolidation keeps reshuffling who's actually making the isotopes.

original_title: AI-ASSISTED GREEN SYNTHESIS OF PHARMACEUTICAL COMPOUNDS: RECENT ADVANCES, APPLICATIONS, CHALLENGES AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES
title: Another lap around AI-for-green-chemistry
blurb: A review rounding up where machine learning has touched greener drug synthesis routes, with the standard tour of advances, applications, and challenges. Good for the citation list, not for new chemistry.
venue: European Journal Pharmaceutical and Medical Research

original_title: Isolation and characterisation of a cadmium-diradical complex: redox non-innocence in d 10 metals
title: A cadmium radical that doesn't fall apart
blurb: Stable cadmium radicals have mostly been theoretical for decades. This isolates and characterizes an actual cadmium-diradical complex showing redox non-innocence, meaning the cadmium itself is carrying some of the electronic load instead of sitting there as an inert d10 center. Solid structural chemistry on a metal that's supposed to be boring.

original_title: A Hydroxyl Radical Model for the S3 State of Photosystem II
title: A hydroxyl radical tucked inside photosystem II's S3 state
blurb: The oxygen-evolving complex's S3 state, the one right before the O-O bond forms, has had years of disputed proposals over Mn oxidation states and oxygen protonation. This adds a new quantum-chemical candidate: a hydroxyl radical bridging a terminal site. It's a calculation, not a measurement, so it's one more model entering an already crowded argument rather than settling it.
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B

original_title: Efficient inverse cobalt-based catalysts for low-temperature methanation of low-concentration CO2 streams
title: Cobalt catalysts for methanating CO2 that's barely even there
blurb: Inverse Ba-REE/Co catalysts (REE = Ce, Nd, or Sm) built for low-temperature methanation of dilute CO2 in hydrogen streams. Putting the promoter oxide on top of metallic cobalt instead of the usual way round maximizes the metal-oxide interface, and the whole series hits 78-84% activity. More about cleaning up hydrogen gas than headline carbon capture.

original_title: Interpretable Machine Learning Accelerates Rational Design of Dual-Site Catalysts for Synergistic Catalytic Aerobic Oxidative Synthesis of Benzimidazole
title: Letting an XGBoost model pick your dual-site catalyst
blurb: Instead of grinding through experimental screening, they trained an interpretable ML model on catalyst descriptors and reaction conditions for aerobic oxidative benzimidazole synthesis, then used partial-dependence plots to read off which compositions and conditions actually help. A sensible shortcut, assuming the model's logic generalizes past this one reaction.

original_title: A Chemical Timer Strategy Programs the Onset of Peroxidase Chemiluminescence
title: A snooze button for peroxidase chemiluminescence
blurb: HRP chemiluminescence normally fires the instant you mix it, which is a problem if your imaging setup isn't ready yet. This adds catechol-type phenolics, protocatechuic aldehyde and protocatechuic acid, as timers that push the onset back anywhere from seconds to minutes depending on concentration. A simple fix for a timing problem that's apparently been annoying people for a while.

original_title: One-Pot Synthesis of Benzofuropyridines and Benzofuroquinolines via Tandem Cycloaddition-Cyclization of Halopyridine- and Haloquinoline N- Oxides with Arynes
title: Arynes plus haloazine N-oxides, straight to benzofuropyridines in one pot
blurb: A transition-metal-free route where chlorinated pyridine or quinoline N-oxides react with in-situ-generated arynes through cycloaddition, rearrangement, and SNAr cyclization in sequence. Where the chlorine sits on the starting N-oxide decides whether you land on the benzofuro[3,2-c] or benzofuro[3,2-b] isomer. Decent regiocontrol for a scaffold that usually takes more steps to reach.

original_title: Directing Cell Fate via Spatiotemporally Patterned Viscoelasticity Driven by Dynamic Crosslink Exchange
title: Tuning matrix viscoelasticity in space and time, not just stiffness
blurb: A dynamic covalent hydrogel with exchangeable crosslinks lets them dial stress-relaxation kinetics up or down, in situ, with light, independent of bulk stiffness. The point is cell fate in 3D tracks viscoelasticity on its own, which is the variable most matrix platforms can't touch.

original_title: Radiopharmaceuticals in Molecular Neuroimaging: Food and Drug Administration-Approved Radiotracers.
title: The FDA-approved radiotracer roster for brain imaging
blurb: A review rounding up the radiotracers actually cleared by the FDA for molecular neuroimaging. Reference material more than a finding.

original_title: Activity and selectivity descriptors for ethylene glycol electrooxidation from first-principle scaling relations
title: A volcano plot for turning PET waste into glycolic acid
blurb: DFT limiting-potential analysis across late transition metals builds a Sabatier volcano for ethylene glycol electrooxidation to glycolic acid, with a simple two-descriptor model explaining why some catalysts beat others. All computational for now, nobody's run the electrode yet.

original_title: Sustainable Synthesis of Novel 3-Trifluoromethyl-benzoxaboroles via Chemometrics and Automation
title: Benzoxaboroles made at room temperature, in open air, by a robot
blurb: DoE optimization lands a sustainable room-temp, open-air route to a new class of 3-CF3 benzoxaboroles, then stretches to heteroaromatic analogs and fresh derivatizations. Porting the whole thing to a robotic platform is the part meant to prove it's not just a fume-hood trick.

original_title: N‐Heterocyclic Carbene‐Catalyzed Atroposelective Monoacylation of Prochiral Diols to Access Axially Chiral Tetraarylethenes
title: An NHC catalyst picks a side on a prochiral diol to build chiral rotors
blurb: NHC-catalyzed desymmetrization monoacylates prochiral diols to deliver axially chiral tetraarylethenes, using cheap starting materials and mild conditions instead of the usual fuss. Worth having since these rotor scaffolds already show up in bioimaging and sensing probes.

original_title: Application of deep eutectic solvents in the synthesis of functional inorganic materials
title: Deep eutectic solvents as reaction media for inorganic synthesis
blurb: A review surveying how deep eutectic solvents get used as the medium for making functional inorganic materials. Light on specifics, more of a field roundup.

original_title: Discovery and development of antimicrobial polymers
title: Antimicrobial polymers get a machine-learning design pass
blurb: A review of antimicrobial polymer development, covering machine-learning-guided design and the push for scalable production so these things can actually be made globally rather than staying a lab curiosity against resistant bugs.

original_title: A Critical Analysis of Spontaneous Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2) Formation at the Air–Water Interface: Reconciling Conflicting Reports
title: Sorting out why water droplets spontaneously make hydrogen peroxide
blurb: A critical review weighing six competing explanations for spontaneous H2O2 formation in microdroplets, from ultrahigh interfacial fields and water comproportionation at the air-water interface to O2 reduction at solid contacts, sonochemistry, and tribochemistry. They referee with their own data plus established radiation and interfacial chemistry rather than add a seventh mechanism to the pile.

original_title: High-Performance Antigen Affinity Chromatography of Monoclonal Antibodies in One- and Multidimensional Configurations
title: Sorting antibody proteoforms by how hard they grip the antigen
blurb: High-performance affinity chromatography separates mAb proteoforms by actual binding strength to their antigen instead of generic charge or size, and coupling it to mass spec lets them pin down which proteoform is dragging down potency instead of just flagging that something's wrong.

original_title: Activity–dissolution trade-offs in multicomponent electrocatalysts
title: Catalysts that work well also tend to dissolve, mapped out
blurb: A framework pairing composition-resolved oxygen reduction activity with electrochemical dissolution measurements across Ag-based alloys, since chasing activity alone just burns through scarce metals faster. The payoff is a map of where a catalyst actually sits on that trade-off, not another activity record.

original_title: DEPI-MS: Density-Equalized Pseudo-Image Learning for Drift-Tolerant LC−MS Metabolomics Classification
title: Stop flattening your metabolomics data into peak tables
blurb: Peak-table workflows for LC-MS metabolomics throw away peak shape, co-elution, and background signal to get down to a handful of numbers. DEPI-MS keeps the whole RT-m/z-intensity field as an image instead, spending resolution where the data actually needs it rather than spreading it evenly, aimed at classification that survives real instrument drift.

original_title: Late-Stage Chemical Editing as a Route to Naturally Occurring Cyclic Tetrapeptides as Selective Inhibitors of Histone Deacetylase 1
title: Late-stage tail-swapping gets you selective HDAC1 inhibitors
blurb: A Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons olefination lets them diversify the tail of a cyclic tetrapeptide scaffold without the usual heavy-metal catalysis, which was enough to total-synthesize two natural products plus two purpose-built oxygenated analogs. All four turn out to be selective HDAC1 inhibitors, though potency varies enough across them that the tail chemistry clearly isn't just decoration.

original_title: Iron-Catalyzed Asymmetric Amino-Pyrazolation of Vinylarenes
title: Iron muscles into pyrazole chemistry that used to need a noble metal
blurb: A one-pot olefin difunctionalization that installs both a primary amino group and a pyrazole across a vinylarene at once, asymmetrically, with iron doing the catalysis instead of the usual two-component noble-metal route. The payoff is a bifunctional amino pyrazole linchpin that's set up for further derivatization, which is really the selling point.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Ammonia-Driven Nanoscale Surface Restructuring of Copper Catalysts during Nitrate Reduction Reaction
title: Watching copper catalysts rearrange themselves while they make ammonia
blurb: Electrochemical AFM catches copper surfaces restructuring in real time during nitrate reduction, and the restructuring tracks the chemistry: moderate overpotentials, where nitrite dominates, spread the terraces laterally, while the regime that dumps out ammonia fast reshapes the surface differently again. The reaction itself seems to be sculpting the catalyst as it runs, not the other way around.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Atroposelective synthesis of lactone-bridged N -arylindoles via Pd-catalyzed formal (6 + 4) cyclization
title: A Pd-catalyzed shortcut to axially chiral N-aryl indoles
blurb: A formal (6+4) cyclization builds the bridged lactone ring and sets the C-N axial chirality in the same step, for a class of bridged heterobiaryl where catalytic atroposelective routes have been scarce.

original_title: Molecular echoes of a hot Earth
title: Your proteins still remember when Earth was way hotter
blurb: Ancestral reconstruction of a transcription factor family finds that ligand binding used to run on entropy back when the planet was hot, and drifted toward enthalpy-driven binding as Earth cooled over billions of years. The thermodynamics of binding carries a record of the climate it evolved under.

original_title: Radical-Based Catalytic Transformations of 1-Azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes: Opportunities and Future Directions
title: Radical chemistry's turn with strained azabicyclobutanes
blurb: A perspective arguing that photoredox, metallaphotoredox, energy-transfer, and electrochemical methods are catching up to classical polar chemistry for prying open 1-azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes into azetidine scaffolds, letting chemists build the sterically crowded C-C and C-heteroatom bonds drug discovery keeps wanting. More of a map of where the field could go than a new result on its own.

original_title: Aqueous [3+2] annulation for modular access to thieno/selenolo[2,3- b ]quinolines
title: Thieno- and seleno-quinolines, built in water
blurb: A thermal [3+2] cyclization that assembles thieno- and selenopheno[2,3-b]quinoline cores in plain aqueous media, a modular route to a scaffold class that usually demands harsher solvent conditions.

original_title: Site‐Selective C–H Alkylation of Arylamines and Unprotected Indoles Enabled by HFIP ‐Mediated Covalently Masked Electrophiles
title: C-H alkylation that skips the directing group and the metal
blurb: HFIP-mediated covalently masked electrophiles do site-selective C-H alkylation on arylamines and even unprotected indoles, the free N-H substrates that usually wreck metal-catalyzed methods needing preinstalled directing groups. The target is triarylmethane cores, common across natural products and materials, built metal-free.

original_title: Computational Fluid Dynamics-Guided Slurry Packing of Capillary Columns for High-Efficiency NanoLC−MS Proteomics
title: Packing LC columns by simulation instead of by hand
blurb: Commercial sub-2 μm C18 packing material is full of fines, aggregates, and a messy particle size spread that wrecks bed uniformity in capillary columns. This builds a CFD model of particle-size-dependent centrifugal transport in a glycerol-water system to sort the particles before packing, so the column bed actually performs like the particle spec claims.

original_title: Preclinical Study Evaluates Lutetium-177 Labeled FAPI in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer - Bioengineer.org
title: Lu-177 FAPI gets a look in triple-negative breast cancer, mice only so far
blurb: FAP-targeted radioligand therapy has been mostly a pancreatic and sarcoma story, now someone's running it in triple-negative breast cancer preclinically. No results to point to yet, just the setup.

I just want to make sure I’m following the correct procedure before proceeding with the organ measurements. original_title: TpPa-1 COF synthesis: Immediate precipitation and solid sticking to the tube walls upon acid addition. How can I avoid this?
title: TpPa-1 COF synthesis: Immediate precipitation and solid sticking to the tube walls upon acid addition. How can I avoid this?
blurb: Hi everyone, I’m currently working on the solvothermal synthesis of TpPa-1 COF and have run into an issue. Has anyone worked with this synthesis before and experienced something similar? original_title: Cathepsin B-Cleavable Voriconazole Macromolecular Prodrugs for Intracellular Release
title: Getting voriconazole past two membranes and into the phagolysosome
blurb: Aspergillus spores hole up inside phagolysosomes, where antifungal drugs have to cross two membranes to reach them and often don't in time. The fix here is a macromolecular prodrug that stays inert until cathepsin B inside the cell cleaves it, dumping voriconazole right where the fungus is hiding.

original_title: Click and Release: How N -Substituted Groups on Hydroxylamine Dictate Click Kinetics and Release Efficiency with Cyclooctynes
title: Tuning the knob on click-and-release chemistry
blurb: Screening N-substituted hydroxylamines against cyclooctynes, they found the N-substituent lets you dial click speed and release efficiency somewhat independently, with some analogues clicking at roughly 10^3 M-1s-1. A toolkit paper for anyone who needs the click and the release running on different clocks.

original_title: Fueling Carbodiimide Chemistry: Direct Structural Characterization of the O -Acylisourea Intermediate
title: The O-acylisourea finally gets its picture taken
blurb: Every carbodiimide coupling, peptide synthesis included, hinges on whether this intermediate reacts productively or collapses into dead-end N-acylurea, and nobody had pinned down its actual structure in over forty years of using it. They finally did.
venue: Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry

original_title: Chemical crosslinking enables profiling of endogenous cell surface galectin-3 interactions
title: Catching galectin-3's cell-surface partners before they let go
blurb: Galectin-3 binds its glycan partners weakly enough that standard pulldowns lose the real interactome in the wash. Crosslinking the complexes in place first, then pulling down and running mass spec, is the workaround, and they're calling it xGL-APMS.

original_title: Proteoform-Resolved Interaction Mapping of Target Protein Complexes in Living Cells via Tracelessly Releasable Cross-Linking.
title: Mapping protein complexes by proteoform, not just by name
blurb: A traceless cross-linking approach for pinning down which specific proteoform, not just which protein, is sitting in a complex inside living cells.

original_title: Normalized membrane ratio of TROP2 as a predictor of clinical outcomes with datopotamab deruxtecan in non-small-cell lung cancer
title: Eyeballing TROP2 under the microscope wasn't going to predict who responds to Dato-DXd
blurb: Standard pathologist IHC scoring of TROP2 doesn't predict response to the ADC datopotamab deruxtecan in NSCLC, so they built a computational scoring system that measures the TROP2 ratio on individual cell membranes instead, and that one actually tracks outcomes.
